currentContext.strategies: Evolve pipeline and portfolio, execute with discipline across markets, and allocate capital thoughtfully to create sustainable long-term value|Build a more differentiated, complexity-led portfolio by sharpening specialized offerings, reinforcing manufacturing reliability, preserving regulatory credibility, and broadening reach of high-quality medicines across geographies|Expand portfolio across complex generics, biosimilars, inhalation therapies, injectables and specialty medicines, segments where scientific complexity creates durable advantage and higher barriers to entry|Expand into novel medicines, including a partnership entered during the year with Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals|Invest ahead of the curve in manufacturing excellence, regulatory capability, supply chain resilience and digital/AI transformation (drug discovery, clinical development, manufacturing operations, commercial decision-making)|Grow India healthcare adjacencies including diagnostics, digital health and consumer healthcare alongside the chronic portfolio|Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI Listing Regulations 43A) outlining the key factors considered by the Board while recommending or declaring dividends; the Board recommended a final dividend for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, and no amount was transferred to reserves during the year. ESG governance is structured with defined roles and accountabilities across the Board, the Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility (SCSR) Committee and senior management, with ESG metrics integrated into executive compensation.
currentContext.expansion: Growth in Other Developed Markets (up 13.3%) was supported by strategic acquisitions including VISUfarma and Renascience, expanding Lupin's footprint outside its core India/US markets. Nanomi (a wholly owned subsidiary) raised its stake in Multicare Pharmaceuticals Philippines, Inc. from 51.0% to 56.3% effective March 30, 2026, part of continued outbound expansion via cross-border investments, partnerships and acquisitions to strengthen market access, regulatory proximity and local presence in priority markets. Lupin is building out Lupin Manufacturing Solutions to capture rising CDMO/CRDMO outsourcing demand, leveraging capabilities in complex chemistry, high-containment APIs, peptides, biologics, antibody-drug conjugates and oligonucleotides. The company is also expanding beyond medicines into diagnostics, digital health, patient-support programs and disease management to augment its chronic and specialty portfolios. On sustainability-linked capital deployment, R&D investment directed toward technologies improving environmental and social impact of products/processes was INR 20,631 million in FY26 (INR 17,672 million in FY25), while the corresponding capex was INR 387 million in FY26 (INR 528 million in FY25). Contracted capital commitments not yet executed rose year-on-year at both the consolidated and standalone level as at 31.03.2026 versus 31.03.2025 (see capex_disclosed), consistent with continued investment in complex and specialty product infrastructure and value-chain oversight.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from patent cliff and genericization
risks.note: As more high-value products lose exclusivity, competition is expected to intensify, increasing the risk of rapid price erosion following launch; success depends on selecting the right opportunities, achieving timely approvals, and maintaining reliable supply.

risks.risk: Geopolitical, currency and market access risk
risks.note: Lupin's presence across multiple geographies exposes the business to currency movements, trade barriers, localization requirements, policy changes, geopolitical disruption and evolving market access requirements, which can affect procurement costs, pricing, supply continuity and profitability.

Growth in complex products, biologics, advanced manufacturing, digital technologies, AI, cybersecurity and global quality systems depends on specialized talent; competition for these skills can affect innovation, operational execution and compliance.

risks.risk: Regulatory/quality compliance execution risk in highly regulated markets
risks.note: The MD&A links manufacturing facility preparedness and engagement with the U.S. FDA to lowering execution risk, raising launch confidence and deepening customer trust — implying inspection/compliance outcomes at manufacturing sites remain a live risk factor in a highly regulated market.

risks.risk: Persistent pricing pressure in commoditized segments (developed markets)
risks.note: In developed markets, while growth is driven by differentiated products, compliance excellence and supply reliability, pricing pressure in commoditized segments is expected to persist, requiring continued portfolio quality and differentiated launches to offset it.

risks.risk: Institutional/tender-led and public-health-funding channel exposure (API Plus)
risks.note: API Plus's institutional sales channels (public health agencies, WHO-linked programs, tender-led markets) are subject to procurement cycles and funding dynamics; the business must navigate funding cycles and institutional demand patterns that are outside its direct control.

one-line thesis: Lupin delivered record Q4/FY26 results driven by a 40% YoY surge in US sales from complex launches (Tolvaptan, Mirabegron), offsetting a one-off $75M settlement cost. Guidance for FY27 moderates to high-single digit revenue and ~25% margins as competition enters key exclusives, though a robust pipeline of biosimilars and the VISUfarma acquisition underpins long-term specialty growth.
financial scorecard: Revenue Q4: INR 7,475 Cr (+32% YoY); FY26: INR 27,958 Cr (+23% YoY). EBITDA Q4: INR 2,171 Cr (+68% YoY, 29.4% margin); FY26: INR 8,160 Cr (+55% YoY, 29.7% margin). PAT not explicitly broken out but ETR 22.1%. One-offs: $75M Mirabegron settlement amortization + variable per-unit costs impacting Q4 margins; lower PLI scheme benefits.
guidance: FY27 Revenue: High single-digit growth (INR terms). FY27 EBITDA Margin: ~25% (down from 29.7% due to competition in Tolvaptan/Mirabegron and higher R&D). R&D spend: ~8% of sales. ETR: 25-26%.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline: 50+ US launches in 3 years (10 first-to-file, 4 biosimilars, 2-3 505(b)(2)s). FY27 launches: Ravicti, Saxenda, Pegfilgrastim (Q2/Q3), Dalbavancin. FY28: Ranibizumab, Dulera, Apixaban 505(b)(2).
segment / subsidiary detail: US: Q4 $371M (+6% QoQ), FY26 $1.32B (+40% YoY). India: Q4 INR 1,908 Cr (+11.5% YoY), Rx +14.5%. Emerging Markets: Q4 +49% YoY (Brazil +113% LC). ODM (Europe/Can/Aus): Q4 +7.1% YoY.
growth verticals / optionality: Biosimilars (Pegfilgrastim, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept, Etanercept) to scale from $50M base; VISUfarma targeting >$100M in 2-3 years; Semaglutide expansion in India/Emerging Markets; Green propellant inhalers.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin improved to 75% (Q4) from 61.7% (Q4FY25) due to mix/cost efficiency. Q4 EBITDA margin pressure from Mirabegron settlement (variable + amortized) and higher manpower. FY27 margin guide ~25% factors in price erosion on key exclusives.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly quantified in Capex line; R&D spend INR 2,063 Cr (FY26, 7.5% sales), guided to 8% FY27. Acquisition of VISUfarma completed.
capital allocation: Net Cash INR 4,636 Cr. Focus on M&A in specialty (Ophthalmology post-VISUfarma, Pulmonology, Rare Neuro) and organic pipeline. No specific buyback/dividend guidance in transcript.
risks & watch-items: Competition entry in Tolvaptan (Sep 2026) and Mirabegron; FDA delays (Ellipta device/PK challenges); Geopolitical freight/raw material inflation (Ocean +15%, Air +60%); PLI scheme reduction.
management quality / tone: Confident on record performance and pipeline depth; Pragmatic on margin compression due to competition; Aggressive on specialty transformation via M&A and biosimilars.
non-obvious takeaways: Mirabegron settlement structure includes both immediate expense and amortization over 2 years; VISUfarma acquisition immediately enables Lupin's respiratory/biosimilar entry into Italy/Spain; Biosimilar franchise currently partner-driven (royalty/profit share) but transitioning to direct sales.

| Price erosion on Tolvaptan/Mirabegron as generics enter | Lupin Limited | loser | Med | Guidance explicitly lowers margins to 25% factoring in this competition, though volume growth may offset some price decline. |

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Persistent pricing pressure in commoditized oral solids is accelerating industry-wide shift toward complex generics, specialty products and differentiated dosage forms (injectables, inhalation therapies, peptides), which Lupin's strategy is aligned to
- Industry entering a significant patent cliff cycle with several blockbuster medicines losing exclusivity through the second half of the decade, expected to accelerate generic and biosimilar adoption
- GLP-1 therapy adoption is expanding the cardiometabolic (diabetes/obesity) market and is expected to transition from innovator-led growth to broader participation by differentiated generics and complex formulations as key molecules approach patent expiry
- Supply chain volatility (API/input-cost inflation, logistics disruption, geopolitical risk, sourcing concentration) is driving industry-wide supplier diversification, regional manufacturing and backward integration
- Biosimilars and advanced modalities (long-acting injectables, antibody-drug conjugates, oligonucleotides, peptides) gaining momentum as healthcare systems seek cost-effective alternatives to biologics
- India pharmaceutical market estimated at approximately USD 60 billion (including exports) in 2026, with long-term projections toward USD 130 billion by 2030, driven by rising healthcare penetration, chronic disease prevalence and wider insurance coverage
- Government initiatives (Production Linked Incentive schemes, bulk drug parks, technology upgradation programs) continue to enhance India's domestic manufacturing depth and innovation capability
- Quality and compliance are becoming competitive advantages as export-oriented pharma models face greater regulatory scrutiny and higher compliance costs
- Approval of Armlupeg (Armlupeg™) in the United States — Lupin's first U.S. biosimilar, following years of investment in biologics research, development and manufacturing
- Launched the generic version of Risperdal Consta®, the first product developed using Lupin's proprietary Nanomi long-acting injectable platform
- Entered into a partnership with Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals during the year as part of expansion into novel medicines (source text truncated before full deal terms/molecule name)

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified global business across United States, India, Europe, Australia, Canada and Emerging Markets, reducing dependence on any single geography
- Global manufacturing network of 15 facilities across multiple geographies providing scale, reliability and flexibility
- Broad portfolio, established presence and reliable supply chain supporting expansion in Emerging Markets through locally relevant products and long-standing institutional partnerships
- Leadership in India's chronic portfolio with market-share gains across key therapy areas and expanding healthcare adjacencies (diagnostics, digital health, consumer healthcare)
- US growth driven by new product launches with exclusivity and continued momentum in inhalation products, reflecting investment in complex products, manufacturing capability and regulatory excellence

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Competition entry in Tolvaptan (Sep 2026) and Mirabegron; FDA delays (Ellipta device/PK challenges); Geopolitical freight/raw material inflation (Ocean +15%, Air +60%); PLI scheme reduction.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Mirabegron settlement structure includes both immediate expense and amortization over 2 years; VISUfarma acquisition immediately enables Lupin's respiratory/biosimilar entry into Italy/Spain; Biosimilar franchise currently partner-driven (royalty/profit share) but transitioning to direct sales.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve pipeline and portfolio, execute with discipline across markets, and allocate capital thoughtfully to create sustainable long-term value
- Build a more differentiated, complexity-led portfolio by sharpening specialized offerings, reinforcing manufacturing reliability, preserving regulatory credibility, and broadening reach of high-quality medicines across geographies
- Expand portfolio across complex generics, biosimilars, inhalation therapies, injectables and specialty medicines, segments where scientific complexity creates durable advantage and higher barriers to entry
- Expand into novel …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price erosion on Tolvaptan/Mirabegron as generics enter | Lupin Limited | loser | Med | Guidance explicitly lowers margins to 25% factoring in this competition, though volume growth may offset some price decline. |
| Supply gaps in Risperdal Consta and complex injectables | Lupin Limited | beneficiary | High | Management cites inability to meet demand due to supply issues at brand/Teva, creating immediate volume upside. |
| Integration of VISUfarma and expansion into new European markets | Lupin Limited | beneficiary | Med | Acquisition adds Euro 50-60M base with 25% margins and cross-sell opportunities for Lupin's respiratory portfolio. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Market entry] China approval for Oseltamivir Phosphate oral suspension in partnership with Yabao Pharmaceuticals, "marking Lupin's first entry into the market".
- [Approvals] Received EMA approval to extend NaMuscla to children aged 6-17 years including two new age and weight appropriate strengths; US FDA approval for Azilsartan Medoxomil Tabs (RLD Edarbi) and Ranibizumab (Ranluspec) biosimilar noted among launches/approvals.
- [Partnership] Launched Luforbec (beclometasone/formoterol) MDI in strategic partnership with Laboratorios ERN S.A. in Spain.
- [Innovation] LNP8701, a novel SOS1 (Son of Sevenless1) inhibitor, had Phase 1a data accepted for publication at ASCO 2026, "reinforcing Lupin's oncology innovation pipeline".
- [IP / filings] As of 31 March 2026: 924 active patent applications, 430 ANDAs and NDAs filed with the U.S. FDA, and 94 US DMF filings.
